TinyWorlds nouns-v2 disjoint benchmark

Every base/task boundary is story-disjoint. Multi-task stories are audited but never used for updates.

2,210,934 clean base stories429,199 pure task stories4,440 validation pairs
Disjoint construction

Zero selected concepts → base; exactly one → its sole task; two or more → permanent exclusion. The base universe covers 81.36% of original training; its optimizer-visible share after the internal holdout is 79.73%.

Sequential controls, independent adapters, and VAMP

One sequential control continually overwrites a rank-eight LoRA; the other fine-tunes every GPT-Neo parameter. Neither receives task identity. The independent control uses a fresh task-matched root LoRA and is a task-aware ceiling. Every row uses the same base, task order, 2,000-update budget, validation stories, midpoint split, and true suffix. Adapter methods use learning rate 1e-3; full fine-tuning uses 5e-5.

Lily and Max were playing in the park with their toy lasers. They liked to pretend they were space heroes, fighting bad aliens. They made loud noises and ran around the slides and swings. But then, the sky became gloomy. Dark clouds covered the sun, and the wind blew hard. Lily and Max felt cold and scared. They heard thunder and saw lightning. They wanted to go home. "Come on, Max, let's go!" Lily said. "It's going to rain soon!" But Max did not want to leave. He liked his laser too much. He said, "No, Lily, I want to play more. My laser is so cool. Look, it can make red lights!" Lily tried to pull Max by the hand, but he shook her off. He said, "Go away, Lily, you are no fun. I don't need you. I have my laser." Lily felt sad and angry. She said, "Fine, Max, be that way. I'm going home. Bye!" She ran to the gate, where their mom was waiting. She told her mom what happened. Her mom hugged her and said, "Don't worry, Lily, Max will learn his lesson soon. Come on, let's go home and prepare some hot chocolate." They got in the car and drove away. Max was left alone in the park. He played with his laser for a while, but then he got bored. He looked around and saw no one. He felt lonely and sorry. He wished he had gone with Lily and his mom. I will do better next time." They got in the car and drove home. Max hoped Lily and his mom would forgive him, too. They liked to pretend they were space heroes, fighting bad aliens. They made loud noises and ran around the slides and swings. But then, the sky became gloomy. Dark clouds covered the sun, and the wind blew hard. Lily and Max felt cold and scared. They heard thunder and saw lightning. They wanted to go home. \"Come on, Max, let's go!\" Lily said. \"It's going to rain soon!\" But Max did not want to leave. He liked his laser too much. He said, \"No, Lily, I want to play more. My laser is so cool. Look, it can make red lights!\" Lily tried to pull Max by the hand, but he shook her off. He said, \"Go away, Lily, you are no fun. I don't need you. I have my laser.\" Lily felt sad and angry. She said, \"Fine, Max, be that way. I'm going home. Bye!\" She ran to the gate, where their mom was waiting. She told her mom what happened. Her mom hugged her and said, \"Don't worry, Lily, Max will learn his lesson soon. Come on, let's go home and prepare some hot chocolate.\" They got in the car and drove away. Max was left alone in the park. He played with his laser for a while, but then he got bored. He looked around and saw no one. He felt lonely and sorry. He wished he had gone with Lily and his mom. He decided to go home, too. He put his laser in his pocket and ran to the gate. But he was too late. The rain started to fall. It was heavy and cold. Max got wet and shivered. He had no umbrella or coat. He had no one to help him. He cried and said, \"Lily, mom, where are you? I'm sorry, I was wrong. I want to go home. Please, come back!\" But no one heard him. He had to wait in the rain until his dad came to pick him up. His dad was angry and worried. He scolded Max and said, \"Max, what were you thinking? You should have listened to Lily and your mom. They were trying to protect you. You were selfish and foolish. You could have gotten sick or hurt. You are lucky I found you.\" Max felt ashamed and sorry. He said, \"I'm sorry, dad, I know I was bad. I won't do it again. I love Lily and mom. I love you, too. Can you forgive me?\" His dad hugged him and said, \"Of course, I forgive you, Max. But you have to learn from your mistake. You have to be kind and respectful to your sister and your mom. You have to be careful and responsible with your toys. You have to be grateful and happy with what you have. Do you understand?\" Max nodded and said, \"Yes, dad, I understand. Thank you, dad. I will do better next time.\" They got in the car and drove home. Max hoped Lily and his mom would forgive him, too. He learned that playing with lasers was not as important as playing with his family. He learned that being gloomy was not as fun as being sunny.
